senses.definition: simple past and past participle of study

quotes.text: He read the letter aloud. Sophia listened with the studied air of one for whom, even in these days, a title possessed some surreptitious allurement.
quotes.reference: 1921, Ben Travers, chapter 1, in A Cuckoo in the Nest, Garden City, N.Y.: Doubleday, Page & Company, published 1925, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (dated) Qualified by, or versed in, study; learned.
examples: He is well studied in theology.

quotes.text: I asked a man well read, well studied in Nietzsche, what the lifelong task was. He could not say. He had only read and studied and loved Nietzsche’s books.
quotes.reference: c. 1969, O. K. Bouwsma, “An Introduction to Nietzsche’s Letters”, in J. L. Craft, Ronald E. Hustwit, editors, Without Proof or Evidence: Essays of O. K. Bouwsma, published 1984, →ISBN, page 122:

quotes.text: I promise, if I wake up as a girl, I will make up for it by having many boys, who will be the most studied and pious boys.
quotes.reference: 2019, Abby Chava Stein, Becoming Eve, Seal Press, page 29:
